{{nihongo|'''Ōnamochi Shrine'''|大名持神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

[[File:Imoyama (Yoshino), enkei.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|View of Imosayama from the opposite bank}}{{small|The torii gate of Daimamochi Shrine is on the center left. In the foreground is [[Yoshino River (Nara Prefecture)|Yoshino River]]. }}]]
``Dainamochi Shrine'' is located in Kawaraya, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}{{ill|Yoshino District, Nara|ar|مقاطعة يوشينو|ceb|Yoshino-gun|es|Distrito de Yoshino|fa|یوشینو|fr|District de Yoshino|id|Distrik Yoshino, Nara|it|Distretto di Yoshino|ja|吉野郡|ko|요시노군|nl|Yoshino (district)|pl|Powiat Yoshino|pt|Distrito de Yoshino|ru|Йосино (уезд)|zh|吉野郡|qid=Q1154558}}{{ill|Yoshino, Nara|Q1203731|qid=Q1203731}}. It is {{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), and {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Old shrine rank}} is {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is also commonly known as ``Daigo Shrine''.{{Sfn|Dainamochi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is located near the junction of the former {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ise Kaido}} and the former Higashi-Kumano Kaido, at the foot of the independent peak {{ill|Imoseyama|Q112339073|qid=Q112339073|lt=Imoseyama}}.

== Enshrined God ==
The following three deities are enshrined. </ref>.
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Daimyochimitamokami}}
* {{ill|Suseri-Hime|Q8191715|qid=Q8191715|lt=Suserihime no Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Shonahikona no Mikoto}}
In the literature, there is ``Daimomichi Shrine'' in ``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'', ``Dainamochi Shrine'' in ``{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'', and ``Engishiki'' extraordinary festival. It is seen as the ``Daimyochimitama Shrine Troupe'' in the Meishin Festival, and the enshrined deity has been one of the troupes of Onamuchi (another name for Okuninushi ({{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944}})).

It is not clear how Sukunabikona (Shona Hikona) was enshrined as a deity, but it was later named after a poem in volume 7 of "{{ill|Man'yōshū|Q834321|qid=Q834321}}" (see below). There is a theory that it is a joint enshrinement of the gods, and another that it is the god of the mountain on the opposite bank. Furthermore, in the "Shinja Detailed Book", there are four deities enshrined: Daimyomochi-kami, Daimyochimitama-kami, the concubine Suserihime-kami, and Shunahikomakami.

== History ==

== Outline ==
Founding date is unknown. {{ill|Imoseyama|Q112339073|qid=Q112339073|lt=Imoyamajuso}} (249 meters above sea level<ref name="Imoyamajuso">[http://www.town.yoshino.nara.jp/kanko-event/meisho-kanko/shisetsu/ryumon-nakaryumon/imoyamajuso.html Imosayama is also called ``Imiyama,'' and it is said to be a sacred mountain because there is a taboo belief against cutting down trees to this day. k|Shintaiyama|Q1595289}} {{ill|Animism|Q43004|qid=Q43004|lt=primitive faith}} is presumed to be the founding shrine {{Sfn|Dainamochi Shrine (gods)|2000}}.In {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=Kokukushi}}, {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=In the year 3 of Tenan}} ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}'s ``Great God'' |Shinkai|Q11591025}} is recorded to the effect that he was promoted from Juichii to Shoichii. At that time, only {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Q714559|qid=Q714559}} in Yamato Province reached the highest rank of Shoichii, which was an extremely early promotion nationwide, but the reason for this is not necessarily clear {{Sfn|Dainamochi Shrine (Shikiuchi)|1982}}{{Sfn|Dainamochi Shrine (Gods)|2000}}. One theory is that it was highly revered because it was an important transportation hub connecting the imperial capital of {{ill|Nara Basin|Q10942269|qid=Q10942269}} to Yoshino {{Sfn|Isenyama/Seyama (Heibonsha)|1981}}.{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extended}} 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) “{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, in Yamato Province {{ill|Yoshino District, Nara|ar|مقاطعة يوشينو|ceb|Yoshino-gun|es|Distrito de Yoshino|fa|یوشینو|fr|District de Yoshino|id|Distrik Yoshino, Nara|it|Distretto di Yoshino|ja|吉野郡|ko|요시노군|nl|Yoshino (district)|pl|Powiat Yoshino|pt|Distrito de Yoshino|ru|Йосино (уезд)|zh|吉野郡|qid=Q1154558}}, ``Daimamochi Shrine Meishin University As a "Monthly Aijo Niiname", it is listed at {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}} and the {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11516161}} and {{ill|Ainame Festival|ja|相嘗祭|simple|Ainame Festival|zh|相嘗祭|qid=Q11581944}} and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}}, it is kept in a heihaku. Also, among the ``Engishiki'' special festivals, the ``Daimyo Mochimitama Shrine Troupe'' can be seen among the 285 Meishin Festivals in the Meishin Festival.

In the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} period, ``Imose Shrine'' can be seen in ``Okami Bunshin Rui Shrine Tsunami Tsukio'' {{Sfn|Dainamochi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}.

In the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}} period, ``Yamatoshi'' shows {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} Daikai-ji Temple (the location of the current shrine office) in the precincts, and a tidal pool in front of the shrine.{{Sfn|Dainamochi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Dainamochi Shrine (Gods)|2000}}. It is said that the tide water gushes out from the Choobuchi, and purification was once performed there {{Sfn|Daimamochi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}.After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, it was ranked as {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} in {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}.{{Sfn|Dainamochi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}In the first year of the Meiji era, Daikai-ji Temple was abolished, the original Buddha and Buddhist utensils were moved to Bukkoku-ji Temple, and the Daihanya Sutra was moved to Unsen-ji Temple.{{Sfn|Dainamochi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}.

== Setsusha ==
[[File:Onamochi-jinja, keidaisha.jpg|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Shinuchisha}}]]
There are the following four companies within the precincts <ref name="Explanation board"/>.
* Wakamiya Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshirosu no Kami}}.
* Water Shrine - Enshrined Deity: {{ill|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|qid=Q8191796|lt=Elephant Goddess}}.
* Konpira Shrine - Enshrined Deity: {{ill|Kanayama-hiko and Kanayama-hime|Q4387856|qid=Q4387856}}.
* Inari Shrine - Enshrined deity: Inasoujin.
